analysis.title: Why volatility may reinforce the commodity case
key_insights: UBS CIO says renewed volatility does not weaken the strategic case for commodities. Differentiated outlooks and return drivers across the asset class could strengthen portfolio resilience.
Markets are reassessing two assumptions alongside the AI trade debate: that Middle East tensions are easing and that the Fed's tightening cycle is nearing an end.

Brent fell as low as USD 89.19 on Tuesday, a two-month low, on more constructive White House comments about potential Iran negotiations. It rebounded to USD 94.7 after Iranian denials of talks and new tanker explosions in the Strait of Hormuz, then settled between the two levels.

A stronger-than-expected October US inflation reading and hawkish comments from several Fed officials moved market pricing back toward further rate hikes. Higher Treasury yields and a stronger US dollar sent gold down nearly 3% on Tuesday to about USD 3,980 an ounce.

Oil supply buffers are limited. Global visible oil inventories were 7.8 billion barrels at end-September, more than 500 million barrels below February pre-war levels, and most pledged strategic reserve releases are complete. UBS thinks current prices are too low relative to the supply outlook.
Record freight costs and constrained tanker capacity mean transport availability, not only production, is shaping the delivered cost of crude.

Gold has structural support. Q3 central bank purchases rose 42% y/y to 321 metric tons (World Gold Council), and ETF inflows of 211 metric tons lifted global holdings to a record above 4,250 metric tons. UBS says elevated real yields and a firm dollar may keep gold volatile near term.

Copper is UBS's preferred industrial metal, supported by power grid, data center, electrification and AI infrastructure investment. The EIA expects US electricity consumption to rise about 3.7% between 2025 and 2027.

Copper supply is constrained. September output at two key Chilean operations fell 21% and 14% y/y, and Shanghai Futures Exchange-monitored stocks fell more than 24% in the latest week to the lowest since January 2024.

UBS favors actively managed, diversified commodity strategies across precious metals, energy, industrial metals and agriculture. It expects Brent at USD 110 by year-end, with unusually high forecast uncertainty, and suggests underallocated investors add gold on pullbacks below USD 4,000.

NVIDIA fell more than 8% after hours on media reports that its board was meeting on whether to potentially remove CEO Jensen Huang, following an investigation into his relationship with a businesswoman and a possible foreign intelligence effort. Nasdaq futures were down 1.1%, Taiwan stocks down 2.8% and South Korea stocks down 1%.

UBS uses the NVIDIA episode to argue for diversification and selectivity as the AI trade matures. It keeps its long-term AI conviction and favors diversified exposure across the AI value chain emphasizing quality, balance-sheet strength, visible monetization and durable free cash flow. It says concentrated tech holders should consider rebalancing across sectors and regions.

market_movers.rationale: Shares fell more than 8% after hours on reports the board was meeting on whether to potentially remove the CEO. UBS takes no view on the company and cites it as a concentration risk.

sector_views.rationale: Low correlation with equities and bonds, limited oil supply buffers, central bank gold buying and constrained copper supply support broad exposure.

Long-term AI conviction is retained, but concentrated positions are exposed to company-specific setbacks and governance and geopolitical risks. UBS favors diversified exposure across the AI value chain.

Tech concentration, governance and company-specific risk from the NVIDIA CEO reports.
Greater scrutiny of advanced-chip exports and supply chains.
vol_and_positioning: Commodity volatility in oil and gold is framed as not weakening the strategic case. Gold fell nearly 3% in one session.
Gold ETF holdings are at a record above 4,250 metric tons after 211 metric tons of inflows.
Nasdaq futures were down 1.1% on the NVIDIA headlines. UBS advises concentrated tech holders to consider rebalancing.
geopolitical: Market reassessing whether Middle East tensions are easing. The White House made constructive comments on potential negotiations with Iran, and Iran denied talks.
New tanker explosions in the Strait of Hormuz. Shipping through the strait remains volatile, costly and exposed to disruption.
Pre-war oil inventory levels (February) are referenced as the baseline. Most pledged strategic reserve releases have been completed.
Potential greater scrutiny of advanced-chip exports and supply chains is cited as a geopolitical risk to technology.
